newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels Bel-20 to remain quiet ahead of Easter.
newsitem.headline: Brussels Bel-20 to remain quiet ahead of Easter.

text.p: The Brussels bourse ended a notch lower on Monday, in what dealers called a dull day as most investors stayed on the sidelines nervously awaiting the U.S. Federal Reserve's FOMC meeting on Tuesday.
Dealers added that trade would remain thin as investors were reluctant to take positions ahead of Easter holidays.
"It was a dull trading day today and this week will remain quiet, the Bel-20 will possibly drop to 2,050," said dealer Benoit Kint at brokerage Petercam.
The blue-chip Bel-20 ended down 0.27 percent, or 5.70 points, at 2,084.03.
Bel-20 volumes were thin with 3.7 billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
"There's no particular story to move the bourse except the FOMC meeting and corporate results due out later this week, which could push shares higher," Kint added.
Click funds which have boosted the bourse in recent weeks were expected to continue coming into the market but in too small quantities to push the Bel-20 much higher.
Dealers said investors were now expecting the Fed to raise U.S. interest rates by 25-basis points and this was reflected in last week's and today's correction.

Investors are eyeing Belgian holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL) which is due to release its 1996 results after bourse close on Tuesday and its Electrafina unit which is likely to release its results on Wednesday.
Electronics group Barco is also expected to release its 1996 results on Wednesday.

Elsewhere pharmaceutical and chemical group UCB fell 2.56 percent to 89,350 francs after the government announced a tax on the turnover of pharmaceutical companies will be increased to four percent from one percent.

Utilities holding company Electrabel fell 0.77 percent to 7,770 francs after the government announced that Electrabel would see the tax on its profits rise to 14 percent from 12 percent as part of an austerity package.
Retailer GIB was the blue-chip's main gainer, closing up 1.63 percent at 1,555 francs, with dealers putting it down to a technical rebound from last week's profittaking.
